audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 fits 49.39% WR over 976 games: Ryze bullies the weak pre-6 Kassadin, and the difficulty comes from converting before Riftwalk stacks scale.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart read Ryze on all seven rows; content (matching packet levelChart) reads Kassadin/Skill/Ryze/Skill/Skill/Ryze/Ryze — rows 0,1,3,4 disagreed.
audit.why: Level 1 is Kassadin's (Q shield blunts the poke opener), 2 and 4-5 are even (he stalls behind Q shields and E slows), 6 is even (Riftwalk dodges W but he cannot burst yet). The blanket-Ryze full chart oversold the stomp.
audit.corrected: Full phases[0,1,3,4].side moved to match content, with why/rating rewrites where the old why argued a Ryze verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: winCon/report[1] said 'shield the burst' — current Ryze has no shield; content whys[0] and early said his Q 'silences you' — Riot's text says Null Sphere interrupts channels, the silence was removed; cooldowns field had no digit; two bullets were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted verbatim; the Nether Blade auto-reset burst tell (missingInteractions) was absent.
audit.why: Ryze passive is bonus-mana damage plus AP-to-mana per the kit file. Kassadin Q: 9-7s CD, magic shield, interrupts channels — no silence in the text. R Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s. W Nether Blade is an auto reset — the wind-up is the burst tell.
audit.corrected: Shield and silence claims removed, cooldowns rewritten with 5s/2s/21s/11s numbers, bleed bullets replaced with kit-grounded bodies including the auto-reset tell.

edits.before: Root the dive, shield the burst, and out-scale him into irrelevance by two items. Keep one eye on Riftwalk and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Root the dive, kite the burst, and starve his stacks into irrelevance by two items. Keep one eye on Riftwalk and one on the wave, in that order.

edits.before: Q-farm at max range — your level 1 is honest at best. Bank Tear stacks and give nothing away.
edits.after: His Q Null Sphere shield eats your poke opener — Q-farm at max range, bank Tear stacks, give nothing.

edits.before: W online: the point-blank root answers anyone who closes. Trade Q-W-Q only when his engage tool is down.
edits.after: W online, but he farms safely behind Q Null Sphere's shield — level 2 evens out; trade when his Q is down.

edits.before: Tear + Lost Chapter and the EQ machine hums — short-trade his every wave contact and walk away before the answer.
edits.after: He stalls with Q shields and E Force Pulse slows through 4-5 — trades even out while he counts down to six.

edits.before: Realm Warp online — you are now a map play waiting to happen. The lane is a timer: shove and warp somewhere profitable.
edits.after: Riftwalk lets him blink out of your W root and roam, but he still cannot burst you — even; track his level-6 roams.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rune Prison has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1, 2s max — too cheap to count late, so win the lane before it ranks up. - E Force Pulse: 21s base, charged by nearby casts — your own spells feed it. - Your W Rune Prison (11s) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: E the wave, Q the flux bounce, and W-root if he steps to answer — three-spell trades that end before his combo starts.
edits.after: Post-6 he Riftwalks past a shoved wave to roam — a centered wave and flank wards turn his blinks into pings, not kills.

edits.before: Spending W on poke and then face-tanking the engage it was born to stop — rootless Ryze is a Tear with a health bar.
edits.after: His combo opens with a W Nether Blade auto reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to step out of E range.

edits.before: Root the dive, shield the burst, and out-scale him into irrelevance by two items. Keep one eye on Riftwalk and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Root the dive, kite the burst, and starve his stacks into irrelevance by two items. Keep one eye on Riftwalk and one on the wave, in that order.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport, always — Ryze is a scaling map champion and TP doubles the thesis. Nothing else is defensible on him.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport, always — Ryze is a scaling map champion and TP extends that plan. Nothing else is defensible on Ryze.

edits.before: Kassadin's Q Null Sphere shields your poke and silences you, edging the first level.
edits.after: Kassadin's Q Null Sphere shield soaks your opening poke trades, edging the first level.

edits.before: Kassadin edges the very first level because Q Null Sphere shields your poke and silences you, denying your Spell Flux setup before you can chain it. But this is a lane you want to be aggressive in; he is one of the weakest pre-6 champions and every CS you deny him delays his power spike. Trade when his Q shield is on cooldown and use minions to avoid eating his E Force Pulse for free. Level 2 evens as you both add a spell and he looks to farm safely.
edits.after: Kassadin edges the very first level because Q Null Sphere pops a magic shield that eats your poke, blunting your Spell Flux setup before you can chain it. But this is a lane you want to be aggressive in; he is one of the weakest pre-6 champions and every CS you deny him delays his power spike. Trade when his Q shield is on cooldown and use minions to avoid eating his E Force Pulse for free. Level 2 evens as you both add a spell and he looks to farm safely.
